model: Sum of the parts: owner FCF DCF on the core EPC and manufacturing business, plus listed IT stakes at market less holdco discount, plus L&T Finance stake at residual income justified price to book (engine route)

equity_bridge.item: LTM (LTIMindtree) stake at market less 20% holdco discount
equity_bridge.note: 203,169,279 shares (FY26 AR investment note, 68.52%) x Rs 4,256.4 (Yahoo LTM.NS, 2026-11-13) = 864.8bn, x 0.80. Full market value would add a further Rs 126/share.

equity_bridge.item: LTTS stake at market less 20% holdco discount
equity_bridge.note: 77,986,899 shares (73.57%) x Rs 4,240.0 (Yahoo LTTS.NS, 2026-11-13) = 330.7bn, x 0.80. Full market value would add a further Rs 48/share.

equity_bridge.item: L&T Finance 65.99% stake at 1.35x book (residual income)
equity_bridge.note: FS segment funds employed Rs 273.2bn at 30-Sep-2026 (Q2 FY27 presentation slide 23) as net worth; justified P/B = (ROE 15% - g 7%) / (CoE 13% - g 7%) = 1.33x, rounded to 1.35x for RoA 2.6% and ROE trending up with 20%+ book growth. 273.2 x 1.35 x 0.6599. Market value of the stake (1,652.5m shares x Rs 277.45) is 458.5bn, ~2.5x book: Rs 156/share more than is counted here.

Group ex-FS NWC/revenue was 19.7% / 16.1% / 12.0% / 11.0% / 4.1% (FY22-FY26) and 1.7% at Sep-2026; 220bn was released in 18 months and sits in the cash counted in net_debt. Management itself calls part of it timing and divestment-related. (6.0% - 1.7%) x ~2,816bn TTM ex-FS revenue. Consistent with wc_capture_pct of -6% on incremental revenue in the base case.

equity_bridge.item: Hyderabad Metro agreed sale consideration (held for sale)
equity_bridge.note: ~Rs 1,461 crore for 100%, agreement 30-Apr-2026, completion now targeted 31-Dec-2026 after three delays. Other Development Projects funds employed (green hydrogen/ammonia, green assets; segment total Rs 151bn, 2.8% return) are NOT counted.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY27 guidance (10-12% group revenue; core P&M ran +11% in H1 and ~+20% in Q2) and Lakshya 2031 (12-15% revenue CAGR), against an order book up 28% YoY to Rs 8.5tn (~3.9x TTM core revenue)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (7.6%) is less than half of revenue CAGR (16.0%) and EPS 3-year CAGR (16.2%): a divergence well over 30%. Book value is held down by the Rs 100bn FY2024 buyback and a ~35-40% payout, not by weak earnings, so equity CAGR is not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Consolidated FY2016-FY2026 (FY ends 31 March). EPS 5-year CAGR is depressed by FY2021, which included the gain on the Electrical & Automation divestment. FCF CAGRs are not reported: consolidated FCF nets NBFC loan disbursements (FY26 119bn, FY23 186bn, FY21 210bn) and the only ex-FS series is the two-year presentation memorandum (FY25 156.1bn, FY26 312.6bn, the latter flattered by a 132.6bn working-capital release). SBC is 0.04% of revenue, so owner FCF and reported FCF are effectively the same series.

scenario_narratives.base: The record Rs 8.5tn order book converts on schedule and core revenue compounds at about 12.6% through FY31, the low-to-middle of the Lakshya 2031 range, then fades to 6% as the Indian public capex and Gulf hydrocarbon cycles mature. Margins stop falling but do not recover much: core EBITDA settles at 8.0% after corporate costs, in line with the ~7.8% PP&M target plus Realty, because the mix keeps shifting toward large fixed-price international energy jobs. About half of the recent working-capital release proves durable; growth then consumes 6% of each incremental rupee of revenue. Part of the new-age investment programme is charged to capex.
scenario_narratives.bull: Lakshya 2031 is beaten the way Lakshya 2026 was: the Rs 10tn prospects pipeline, Middle East reconstruction, defence indigenisation and nuclear/SMR orders hold growth at 14-16% for five years. Hi-Tech Manufacturing (15-17% margin) grows as a share of the mix and legacy water and early-stage CarbonLite/offshore-wind jobs cross their margin-recognition thresholds, lifting core EBITDA to 8.8%. Customer advances on international hydrocarbon work keep working capital structurally low (3% of incremental revenue).
scenario_narratives.bear: The West Asia conflict or a lower oil price stalls Gulf awards (one-third of revenue, 40% of the order book) while Indian government capex slows, so growth drops to 3-6% from FY29. Chinese and Korean price competition and cost overruns on fixed-price jobs take core EBITDA below 7%, the path the water projects are already on. Working capital reverts toward its historical double-digit share of revenue (10% of incremental revenue), and the new-age capex (green hydrogen, data centres, semiconductors) earns nothing while running at 2.5% of revenue.

valuation_philosophy.summary: L&T is three kinds of business under one ticker, so it is valued as three. The core contractor is an owner-FCF DCF on its own revenue, margins, capex and working capital, with its own net cash. The listed IT subsidiaries enter at what L&T's shares would fetch in the market less a 20% holding-company discount, and the NBFC at a residual-income multiple of book rather than its much higher market price. Nothing is counted twice: subsidiary cash, NBFC borrowings and minority interests stay with the subsidiaries. SBC is immaterial, so the house and street bases coincide and the band has collapsed (band_position is not meaningful).
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is about 61% of the core's enterprise value, and a 1pt move in WACC moves the core by roughly 15% (about Rs 220-230 per share). Even at an 11% INR discount rate the base value stays well below the market price, so the gap is not a discount-rate artefact alone.
The equity bridge is scenario-invariant. LTM and LTTS are taken at market price, so a de-rating of Indian IT services flows straight through at about Rs 7 per share for every 1% move in their prices.

Working capital: 220bn was released in 18 months. The model treats about 121bn of it (Rs 88 per share) as temporary; each 1pt of NWC/revenue that does or does not reverse is worth about Rs 20 per share.
The Rs 430-450bn new-age investment programme is mostly outside the model on an NPV-neutral assumption. If it earns below its cost of capital the cash pile counted here is overstated.
Core EBITDA margin: 0.5pt on the terminal margin moves terminal-year FCF by roughly 8%.
L&T Finance is held at 1.35x book against a market price of ~2.5x book; using market would add ~Rs 156 per share.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of for LT.NS; 52-week range 3,288.1-4,440.0. LTM.NS, LTTS.NS and LTF.NS from the same endpoint, same date.
data_sources.financials: LT.NS_Metrics.csv and kpis (consolidated, INR millions); Q2/H1 FY27 earnings presentation (27-Oct-2026: balance sheet, cash breakup, ex-FS cash flow, segment EBITDA, return ratios); Q4 FY26 presentation (FY26 segment details, working-capital ratios, ex-FS cash flow); FY2026 annual report (subsidiary shareholdings, standalone lease cash flows).
data_sources.qualitative: LT.NS_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): Lakshya 2031 targets, FY27 guidance, segment trends, bull/bear points.

inputs.share_count_basis: 1,375.9m shares on issue at 30-Sep-2026 grossed up by the H1 FY27 basic/diluted EPS gap (67.78 vs 67.76, ~0.03%) = 1,376.3m fully diluted. Held flat: no SBC of note in the core and no non-SBC issuance planned.
inputs.net_debt_note: CORE ONLY, 30-Sep-2026, Q2 FY27 presentation slides 26-27. Cash and current investments: Standalone 455bn + Other Subsidiaries 197bn = 652bn. EXCLUDED: LTM & LTTS 187bn (inside their market values in the bridge) and L&T Finance 135bn (inside its book value). Debt: 'Borrowings - Others' 130bn; EXCLUDED: Financial Services borrowings 1,233bn (operating funding of the NBFC, not net debt). Lease liabilities excluded (treatment B). Consolidated cash of 974bn in the Metrics CSV is NOT the right anchor for this model.
inputs.fcf_note: FY2026 memorandum cash flow EXCLUDING Financial Services (Q4 FY26 presentation slide 38): net cash from operations 354.9bn less net investment in fixed assets 42.3bn. This is not a normal year and not the projection base: it carries a 132.6bn working-capital release (NWC/revenue 11.0% -> 4.1%) and includes the IT subsidiaries. The consolidated FCF in the Metrics CSV (119.3bn) is after 2.3tn-scale NBFC loan disbursement flows and is meaningless for valuation. The forward build starts from core revenue and components, not from this figure.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest and dividends received (29.0bn FY26 ex-FS) are classified in investing, so they are not inside reported_fcf and nothing needs stripping from it. Forward flows are built from segment EBITDA with no treasury income; the cash that earns it is in net_debt (matching-asset rule).
inputs.sbc_source: Consolidated cash flow statement FY2026 share-based payment add-back (Metrics CSV), 0.04% of revenue and almost entirely LTM/LTTS ESOPs, which sit outside the core flows. Core SBC modelled explicitly at 0%. No net-share-settlement tax line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0).
inputs.buyback_note: No repurchase since the Rs 100bn tender buyback in FY2024. Flat count is not being 'funded' by buybacks, but there is no SBC dilution in the core to fund.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T09:58:09Z (15:28 IST Friday, regular NSE session; stock up ~13% since the 27-Oct Q2 result)
inputs.wacc_rationale: INR-built: India 10-year G-sec ~6.5% + ~5.5% equity risk premium x beta ~1.0 = ~12.0% cost of equity. The core carries net cash, so WACC = cost of equity = 12.0%. Same rate in all three scenarios; risk lives in the flows and the weights, not in per-scenario discount rates. Terminal growth 5.5% base = ~4% RBI inflation target + ~1.5% real.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Standalone lease principal 2.35bn + lease interest 0.49bn (FY2026 cash flow statement) = 2.84bn, ~0.14% of core revenue, charged in the flows via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities excluded from net debt; da_pct_path is ex right-of-use depreciation (core D&A 21.4bn FY26 less ~2.3bn ROU = ~0.9% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged once, by construction. LTM, LTTS and L&T Finance are NOT in the flows; only L&T's own shareholding enters the bridge (203.17m LTM shares, 77.99m LTTS shares, 65.99% of L&T Finance), so the minorities' share is never counted. NCI inside the core (P&M) is immaterial (Rs 9 crore of Q2 FY27 PAT) and ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: sum of the parts, because the business straddles three rows of the dcf-methods routing table. (1) Core = Projects, Products & Manufacturing + Realty (old 'Projects & Manufacturing' aggregate, FY26 net revenue Rs 2,099.8bn, EBITDA 8.3%): owner-FCF component DCF, non-US/cyclical adaptations. (2) LTM (LTIMindtree) and LTTS: separately listed, majority-owned; L&T's shares at market price on 13-Nov-2026 less a 20% holding-company discount. (3) L&T Finance (NBFC): deposits/borrowings are operating funding, FCF is meaningless, so residual-income justified P/B on book, not FCF and not market. A consolidated owner-FCF DCF would treat Rs 1.2tn of NBFC borrowings as net debt and loan disbursements as negative FCF. Development Projects (FY26 revenue 51bn, Nabha Power sold June 2026, Hyderabad Metro held for sale) and the TPS 'Others' new-age units (data centres, semiconductor design) are excluded from the flows; only the agreed Hyderabad Metro consideration is in the bridge. The equity bridge is scenario-invariant in the engine, so bear/base/bull differ only in the core; the subsidiaries' own upside/downside is not flexed. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). Price not after-hours.

base.margin_note: Core (P&M incl. Realty) segment EBITDA was 8.3% in FY26 and 7.4% in H1 FY27 against 7.7% in H1 FY26, pointing to ~8.0% for FY27; 0.3pt is held back for unallocated corporate cost, which the segment table nets against treasury income in 'Corporate'. Management's PP&M target is ~7.8%.
base.capex_note: Core capex ran ~1.4% of revenue in FY26 (ex-FS net fixed-asset investment 42.3bn less ~12bn at the IT subsidiaries). The path charges a further ~0.4pt early for the Rs 430-450bn Lakshya 2031 new-age programme; the remainder of that programme is assumed NPV-neutral and neither its cash nor its revenue is in the model.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: the core is a cyclical fixed-price contractor with a third of revenue in an active conflict region, and margin compression is already in the reported numbers rather than hypothetical. Base 50%: guidance, the order book and Lakshya 2031 all point at this path. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs sustained mid-teens growth, a margin recovery and durable negative working capital at the same time, three things that have not coincided in the last decade.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
